title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages, pp. 405-406 of the original numbering). Grothendieck works with a profinite group M_{0,3}^{!~}. It is an extension of an arithmetic group N_{0,3}^{!~} by the geometric profinite fundamental group π_{0,3}^∧ of U_{0,3} = P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. Here N_{0,3}^{!~} is essentially Γ_Q = Gal(Qbar/Q), enlarged by the S_3 of automorphisms permuting 0, 1, ∞. On the previous page he has described elements of N^{!~} by pairs (α,β) satisfying a 'loop equation' (97). This is a precursor of the GT relations. Group law: cocycle formulas (125).

This page. For each algebraic point q of U_{0,3}, the rational point q (over k_q = Q(q)) gives a partial section K_q of the extension. Let Γ_Q(q) be the stabilizer of q (the decomposition group, i.e. Gal(Qbar/Q(q)) when q is in Qbar). Then K_q is a section over Γ_Q(q), or over its enlargement M^{!~}(q) inside N^{!~} once the S_3-stabilizer of q is included. It is well defined only up to π-conjugacy, a 'packet' of partial sections. M^{!~}(q) denotes the hypothetical subgroup of M^{!~} that is the image of this section. It should map onto Γ_Q(q).

The special points:
- q = 1/2 is fixed by z -> 1-z and is rational, so Γ_Q(q) = Γ_Q.
- q = -j (a primitive 6th root of unity) is fixed by the order-3 rotation ρ. Its stabilizer is Gal(Qbar/Q(√-3)), the index-2 kernel of a quadratic character ε∘χ of the cyclotomic character χ: Γ_Q -> Ẑ^*.

He says the earlier case analyses '1° and 2°' (presumably exploiting the order-2 and order-3 symmetries) amounted to determining these splittings. Transporting by ρ turns K_{1/2} into K_2 and K_{-1}, the S_3-orbit of 1/2. Transporting K_{-j} by a transposition τ gives K_{-j̄}, since 1-(-j) = -j^2. He then turns to M^{!~}[0], attached to the cusp 0 (continued on the next page). Its intersection with π is the inertia/loop group L_0, so it is not a section. A choice of uniformizer at 0 splits it, i.e. a tangential base point. He proposes interpreting this splitting as a privileged normalization of (α,β) mod L_0.

The left margin explains that Γ_Q(q) is implicitly defined for q algebraic over Q, via its image under Γ_Q(q) -> Ẑ^* compared with Γ_Q -> Ẑ^*.

Purpose: use the Galois sections attached to the S_3-symmetric points 1/2 and -j, and the cusps, to constrain or normalize the solutions (α,β) of the loop equation. In other words, derive GT-type relations from points with extra automorphisms.
errors: The stabilizer of -j corresponds to Q(√-3) = Q(μ_3), i.e. the character Ẑ^* -> (Z/3)^* = {±1}. Writing it as 'ε_2∘χ' is suspicious unless ε_2 is earlier notation for the mod-3 sign character. Mod 4 would give Q(i), the wrong field.
The sections K_q are only defined up to π_{0,3}^∧-conjugation (a packet), and over k_q rather than over Q. Grothendieck acknowledges this ('un amas de scindages', 'sous-groupe hypothétique').
Transporting by τ: the transpositions send -j to -j̄ (not to -j), consistent with the orbit {-j, -j̄}. Transcribing the result as 'K_{-j}' would be wrong; it should be K_{-j̄}.

ideas.what: Partial sections of the arithmetic fundamental group extension of P^1-{0,1,∞} attached to algebraic points q, defined over the decomposition group Γ_Q(q)
ideas.modern_name: Galois sections from rational points (section conjecture setting)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983); standard in anabelian geometry
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme (1984) in spirit

ideas.what: Using the S_3-symmetric points 1/2 (with orbit 2, -1) and -j (with orbit -j̄), whose stabilizers involve S_3 elements, to obtain constraints on the Galois action / loop equation
ideas.modern_name: Eigenloci / special points with automorphisms giving GT-type relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps (1997, 'On a new version of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group'); H. Nakamura on Galois action at special points

ideas.what: Cusp 0: the subgroup M[0] meets π in the loop group L_0; a uniformizer at 0 splits it, to be used as a normalization of (α,β) mod L_0
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions tangential base points informally

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly frames his case analyses of the loop equation as the determination of Galois sections at the S_3-fixed points q=1/2 and q=-j, transported by S_3. This anticipates using points with nontrivial automorphism stabilizers to derive Grothendieck-Teichmüller relations, the strategy later found independently by Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps.
missed.quote: L'analyse des cas 1° et 2° ci-dessus revenait en fait à la détermination de tels scindages, pour q=1/2 et pour q=-j
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's priority for the 'special points' approach to GT-relations at the M_{0,4} level. It also suggests a systematic program, never completed, of computing the sections K_q for all S_3-special and CM-like points.

missed.claim: Proposed but undeveloped: interpret the tangential splitting at a cusp, attached to a uniformizer, as a canonical normalization mod L_0 of the loop-equation data (α,β).
missed.quote: il faudra dans la suite essayer de saisir un tel scindage ... comme une façon privilégiée ... de 'normaliser' le choix de (α,β) mod L_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This corresponds to normalizing GT elements via tangential base points (as in Drinfeld/Ihara's f_σ). It is only a sketch here.

deep.surprise_reason: The ideas (Galois sections at rational points, tangential base points, special symmetric points) are known in later literature. Still, the explicit link between the S_3-special points 1/2, -j and solving the loop equation is an early, unpublished anticipation of the Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps approach.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 probably reads 'dont au moins un amas de scindages partiels au dessus de Γ_Q(q)' rather than 'des moins'.
'en transformant par l'un quelconque des τ_i' (not τ_ρ); the struck phrase also refers to τ_i.
'un scindage de type K_{-j̄}' (bar on j), i.e. the conjugate point -j̄.
'et idem pour M_{0,3}^{!~}(q)' with insertion 'et ρ' above, meaning the stabilizer in the enlarged group also contains ρ.
The margin begins 'La définition implicite lorsque q est élément d'une extension algébrique de Q ...'; the rest is largely illegible.
